NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang speaks to US President Donald Trump, as US House Speaker Mike Johnson (centre) looks on, at the White House driveway following a luncheon for tech leaders in the East Room, in Washington, DC, US, on Sep 29, 2026. (File photo: Reuters/Kevin Lamarque)

WASHINGTON: United States House Speaker Mike Johnson said on Thursday (Nov 12) there was growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China after a spy scandal forced out Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang . Huang stepped down after reports of a romantic relationship with a businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for the Chinese government.  Lawmakers from both parties have since called for tougher restrictions on China's access to advanced artificial intelligence chips, threatening access to chips that underpin China's surging AI development. Nvidia's advanced AI chips are widely used to develop cutting-edge AI models, making the company key to the US race against China to build superior AI systems. The US has sought for years to limit China’s access to Nvidia’s chips because it does not want the Chinese military to benefit from them.

"The export controls on chips to China has been a big issue around here," Johnson, a Louisiana Republican, told reporters at the US Capitol, adding he favoured limiting China's access to the advanced technology.  "I think there's a developing consensus in Congress that is an important position to take." The Chinese businesswoman, Alice Huang, was an executive at Megaspeed , an Nvidia partner the US government suspects of helping China obtain advanced AI chips restricted under US export controls. Beijing has denied Alice Huang is a spy.

Related:

Who is Alice Huang, Chinese exec accused of spying on Nvidia CEO?

Commentary: Everything Jensen Huang said about China is out the window

REPUBLICANS EYE EXPORT RESTRICTIONS The case has revived claims among China critics in Washington that US export policies are too weak, boosting calls for more restrictions. Reuters reported that Chinese AI companies are trying to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity outside China because they are worried the Jensen Huang allegations could spur Washington to tighten restrictions on their ability to access the company's chips remotely.   Congressional Republicans are keen to attach new restrictions on exporting advanced AI chips to China in the annual defence authorisation Bill, a must-pass measure that funds the military and typically attracts bipartisan support, according to a Senate aide, who spoke on the condition of anonymity.  Lawmakers are pressing their colleagues to pass at least four Bills on chip exports, according to statements since Monday.  The AI Overwatch Act would give Congress more power over advanced AI chip exports. The Chip Security Act would require companies to track the location of advanced AI processors to prevent smuggling.  The Match Act would pressure US allies to restrict sales and maintenance of advanced chipmaking equipment destined for China. The Remote Access Security Act would give the Commerce Department the tools to stop Chinese firms from renting overseas data centres to access Nvidia chips. Jensen Huang is separately expected to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving, which falls on Nov 26.  House Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast, a Florida Republican, told reporters on Thursday that congressional staff spoke with Nvidia on Wednesday night about a date and location for his testimony.  Mast and two other leading House Republicans asked Huang last week to brief them behind closed doors about his relationship with the suspected Chinese spy.

ANTALYA: World leaders have set out competing positions and made clashing demands in two days of intense speech-making at the COP31 climate change talks in Türkiye , leaving negotiators with a tough task to draft a meaningful deal that all can agree. Small island states, among the most vulnerable in the world as global warming makes sea levels rise, pleaded for urgent cuts to greenhouse gas emissions. European leaders , meanwhile, lined up behind a proposal to expand global electrification, developing countries asked for more finance from rich ones, and fossil fuel producers said oil, gas, and coal should continue to be used. "We reaffirm our sovereign right to strengthen our energy and oil industry as a driver of our national development," Venezuela's acting President Delcy Rodriguez told the conference, after UN leaders had made the case for bringing to an end the age of fossil fuel.

Apart from trying to accommodate incompatible national positions aired on Wednesday (Nov 11) and Thursday (Nov 12), conference host Türkiye and negotiations lead Australia also have the challenge of trying to make progress when wars and inflation have pushed climate concerns down the political agenda. "It's my job to steer consensus, not to bang tables and demand any particular action, but to steer consensus to the strongest , most ambitious possible out come within the constraints of that consensus-driven process," Chris Bowen, Australia's COP31 president of negotiations , told Reuters. Asked what a good deal might look like, he said: "I have many more hours of consultations with partners to do." Climate activists say short-term political concerns should not get in the way of addressing an issue that will get more pressing if ignored. A UN report last month found the world was already on course to break through the 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) warming limit that countries had agreed to pursue under the 2015 Paris Agreement to prevent the worst effects of climate change. "The situation could not be less under control. The planet is not dying. It is being killed," Swedish climate activist Greta Thunberg said on the sidelines of the UN conference. "It is being killed by the very same people often thought to come to our rescue. No one is coming to our rescue."

BRITAIN'S BURNHAM BACKS RENEWABLES Earlier on Thursday, the leaders of small island states including the Bahamas, Tuvalu, the Solomon Islands and Saint Lucia called for swift action. "Major emitters must move beyond the usual promises. They must reduce emissions that the climate crisis demands," said Saint Lucia's Prime Minister Philip J . Pierre. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham backed a proposal by Turkey to increase electricity's share of world energy consumption to 35 per cent by 2035, from a little over a fifth now, to help advance that goal. Turkey has not specified whether the extra energy used would be renewable. Burnham told the conference that energy supply disruptions from the US-Israeli war with Iran and Russia's war with Ukraine showed clean energy was the wise choice. "It is now plain for everyone to see that if we depend on energy we do not control, then we leave ourselves exposed to prices we cannot control," he said. "The shift to clean energy is the only r out e to energy security." Developing countries reiterated requests that they have made during many years of UN talks for rich countries to provide more finance to help them shift to cleaner energy, adapt to a warming world , and repair climate-driven destruction. Fernanda de Carvalho, the head of climate policy for the World Wildlife Fund environmental group, said he found the leaders ' speeches underwhelming, especially as COP31 i s the first UN conference since scientists have publicly said the world is set to breach the 1.5C threshold. "It is worrying that the climate issue is not as high on the global political agenda as it needs to be," he said.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stepped down on Thursday (Nov 12) after revelations of two extramarital affairs , including one involving a suspected Chinese spy , plunged the chipmaker into crisis and sent shockwaves across an AI industry he helped bankroll. Huang's exit caps a tumultuous week for Nvidia , one of the major engines behind the AI boom, and could have far-reaching consequences for US chip export policy and the broader AI ecosystem, given the ex-CEO's push to preserve access to the Chinese market, as well as his close ties with US President Donald Trump. The crisis has threatened to implicate some Trump administration members, including Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is facing growing questions over the administration's oversight of chip sales to China, particularly as both he and Huang pushed for relaxing those sales despite scrutiny from longtime China hawks in both parties. The Commerce Department did not immediately comment. Senior White House officials are discussing whether Lutnick should be pushed out, two people familiar with the situation told Reuters on Thursday.

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Lutnick's future. Earlier in the day, a White House official said US President Donald Trump "maintains complete confidence in the secretary and his ability to carry out the position." Huang's departure threatens to disrupt an AI ecosystem that he helped shape by pouring Nvidia 's swelling cash pile back into cloud providers, suppliers and the industry's biggest labs. The surge in AI computing demand drove a sevenfold increase in Nvidia 's shares through early October, pushing its market value at one point to nearly US$6 trillion. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor, considering both internal and external candidates, the company said on Thursday.

Related:

Who would be next CEO at Nvidia? Top engineer and CFO favoured as candidates

Jensen Huang scandal could spur tighter US scrutiny of AI cloud providers in Southeast Asia: Analysts

The departure has also ignited speculation over who will ultimately lead the company, long associated with the leather-jacket-wearing Huang, who co-founded Nvidia more than three decades ago. Kress and longtime Nvidia engineer Ian Buck had emerged as the leading internal candidates among investors and analysts even before Huang's departure. Nvidia shares were down about 4.8 per cent, paring earlier losses. Shares of rivals AMD and Broadcom rose about 6 per cent each. Huang, Nvidia 's fourth-largest shareholder with a 3.61 per cent stake, will also leave the board. Nvidia named former Synopsys CEO and longtime director Harvey Jones as its first board chair. "The Board, Estaff (executive staff) and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period," Kress wrote in a memo to employees, adding that the company will host a meeting on Nov 18. Kress was gathering Nvidia 's executive team at its headquarters on Thursday, CNBC reported, adding that Huang had agreed to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving. Huang has hired law firm Paul Weiss, the New York Times reported, citing two people familiar with the matter. It was not clear what the firm had been retained to do, the report said. The company has not commented beyond its statement announcing Huang's resignation. REPLACING HUANG Pressure had been mounting on Huang in recent days after reports said the 63-year-old, who is married, had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing. The New York Times also reported Wednesday that Huang had an extramarital affair with a senior company executive who reported to him. While Kress offers investors a familiar hand after 13 years as CFO, analysts have pointed to Buck as a potential longer-term candidate because of Nvidia 's reliance on technical leadership. The veteran engineer helped develop its crucial CUDA software platform and now leads its hyperscale AI products. "The risk is not that Nvidia suddenly loses its technology roadmap ... that roadmap is largely visible for the next several years. The risk is execution. Jensen has been the chief conductor of an extraordinarily complex system," said Michael Feldman, portfolio manager at ClearBridge Investments. "In a world with real bottlenecks, that coordination is a competitive advantage in itself." Investor sentiment toward AI stocks has already been shaky as soaring cash burn and rising debt at traditionally cash-rich tech giants fuel doubts over whether the AI boom will pay off.

TRUMP WEIGHS IN Trump said on Sunday that Huang had "done an amazing job for our country" and that the Nvidia chief had told him he had no idea the Chinese woman he had an affair with was a spy. Trump had urged Huang to fight for his job in a call on Tuesday, the New York Times reported. On Thursday, the US president suggested former Apple CEO Tim Cook should take over as Nvidia 's CEO. US House Speaker Mike Johnson said it was "critically important for right successor to be chosen to replace Huang", noting there was a growing consensus in Congress on limiting exports of semiconductor chips to China. HUANG'S ROCK-STAR STATUS For years, Nvidia was best known to gamers chasing top-tier graphics. But its chips' ability to perform many calculations at once has made them the oil of the AI boom and a strategic prize in the US-China race to dominate the technology. It also made Nvidia the world's most valuable company. That turned Huang into a rock-star CEO, mobbed by fans in Taiwan and South Korea who ask him to sign books, posters and sometimes even their bodies. The scandal preceding Huang's departure unfolded over more than a year, beginning with an October 2025 New York Times report linking him to Alice Huang , a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a coveted official Nvidia cloud partner with priority access to its chips. Subsequent reports said US intelligence officials believed Alice Huang was acting on behalf of Chinese intelligence. Beijing has denied Alice Huang is a spy. Washington has also investigated Megaspeed over suspicions it helped China obtain advanced AI chips restricted under US export controls, according to media reports.

Related:

Alice Huang barred from re-entering Singapore; insufficient evidence she committed offences in Megaspeed probe: MHA

What we know about Megaspeed, Singapore-based customer of Nvidia

Separately, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday that the US Justice Department was investigating Alice Huang over whether entities linked to her were involved in efforts to smuggle Super Micro Computer products to China, citing a person familiar with the matter. A spokesperson for the Manhattan US Attorney’s office declined to comment on the Bloomberg report. The office previously charged three people associated with Super Micro, including its co-founder, with helping smuggle at least US$2.5 billion of US AI technology to China in violation of export laws. Super Micro did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Earlier, the Singapore Ministry of Home Affairs said Singapore police had been investigating Super Micro as part of a wider probe into Megaspeed and Alice Huang. The police had reached out to the FBI and the Justice Department for help and had received "limited information or assistance," the ministry said. Earlier this month, Nvidia 's board launched a probe, led by independent directors with outside legal counsel, into whether Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. It also expressed confidence in him at the time. The controversy escalated on Wednesday when the New York Times reported Huang also had an affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia 's vice president of healthcare, who reported to him.

Source: Reuters/sz/fs

NEW YORK: The death toll from a residential building collapse in New York rose to at least eight, including two children, on Thursday (Nov 12), after more bodies were recovered from the rubble, officials said.

Rescuers worked through the night, searching the site in the Flatbush neighbourhood of Brooklyn where the three-story building collapsed on Wednesday.

They recovered four more bodies overnight, while two others died in the hospital, Fire Chief Lillian Bonsignore told a news conference.

That brought the death toll to eight, including two children, New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said, adding that another 19 people were injured and one is in critical condition.

"This has been a devastating morning and evening for our city," he said.

Shop worker James Williams, 60, said he witnessed the building collapse after hearing loud banging noises throughout the morning.

"I smelled the smoke from the fumes, and I was watching bricks fall. But to see, like two minutes later, to see the building collapse and fall, it was just devastating," he told AFP.

"There were people trying to get out ... I saw somebody on the side of the staircase, and I'll be honest with you, I didn't even really want to think about that."

Members of the New York City Fire Department and first responders search for victims in the rubble a day after a building collapsed in Brooklyn in New York on Nov 12, 2026. (Photo: AFP/Charly Triballeau)

Another witness, 14-year-old Kenneilia Reid, told AFP: "When I was walking by, I started seeing dust all of a sudden, and I was like, what is going on? When I turned my back, I saw the whole building collapse."

The building, a three-story structure dating from 1930 with four apartments and a commercial space on the ground floor, collapsed onto a nearby excavation site.

A massive emergency response was launched, with about 250 firefighters and rescue workers and search dogs on site.

An adjacent building was also affected, with one of its walls torn away, leaving a staircase and rooms exposed on the rubble.

The cause of the collapse was not immediately clear, and firefighters continued to work at the site on Thursday. STOP-WORK ORDER "My stomach hurts. I can't imagine you were just in your kitchen doing something" and then "you're not any place. It's crazy," Annemarie, a 60-year-old care worker who did not want to share her last name, told AFP. She lives on the street behind the collapsed building.

"It could have been me, you know, it's really scary," she said.

The building fell into an adjacent work site, where construction workers had been excavating, Ahmed Tigani, commissioner of New York's Department of Buildings, told a press conference late Wednesday.

Tigani said that developers had plans approved for a three-story building at the site and were pursuing permission for a nine-story building.

Members of the New York City Fire Department and first responders search for victims in the rubble a day after a building collapsed in Brooklyn in New York on Nov 12, 2026. (Photo: AFP/Charly Triballeau)

According to documents from the city's building department reviewed by AFP, the construction site had been issued a stop-work order in April due to potentially dangerous demolition conditions.

However, work continued, resulting in a US$10,000 fine for the company involved. No link has yet been established between these violations and the building's collapse.

Mamdani said five main entities were involved at the site and authorities on Thursday started "sweeping" 100 other construction sites they are associated with around the city.

The mayor promised a thorough investigation and to hold anyone responsible "fully accountable."

The city's Department of Buildings said its inspectors were on the scene "assisting with recovery operations and conducting structural stability inspections of nearby buildings."

Source: Reuters/as

Global AI-linked stocks tumbled on Thursday as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned following a deepening scandal around his affairs, upending the chipmaker's leadership and posing fresh risks to a sector already reeling with funding and regulatory concerns. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor, the company said. As the centrepiece of the AI ecosystem, the chipmaker finances infrastructure built around its chips - a strategy that has drawn scrutiny over circular funding and now risks weighing on the sector as its crisis deepens. Nvidia's shares fell 8.2 per cent to a more than 16-month low in early trading and its market value was on track to close below US$4 trillion for the first time since July 2025.

"Nvidia has been called the 'Bank of AI'. If they have to take a step back because of what's going on, will that cut off funding to smaller companies that need it? That's an open question," said Joe Saluzzi, partner and co-head of equity trading at Themis Trading. Nvidia-backed neocloud firm CoreWeave dropped 9.1 per cent after surging more than 27 per cent in the previous session when its earnings ignited a relief rally in AI stocks. Other neocloud stocks, including IREN and Applied Digital, were also trading lower. Nebius dropped 16.2 per cent after the company said its 2026 revenue would come in at the low end of its previous forecast. Nvidia has lost more than US$550 billion in market value since the board announced an investigation on Sunday into Huang's relationship with a businesswoman called Alice Huang, who is alleged to be a Chinese spy. "The interlocking deals that Nvidia has with so much of the industry raises the question into whether that created more stability or more fragility. We're going to find out over the next few weeks as this whole situation unravels," said Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers. Nvidia short sellers have made US$9.6 billion in on-paper profits so far this week, according to data analytics firm ORTEX.

Related:

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid deepening scandal, leaving AI chip giant at crossroads

Jensen Huang scandal could spur tighter US scrutiny of AI cloud providers in Southeast Asia: Analysts

Nvidia, CEO Jensen Huang sued over disclosures related to suspected Chinese spy

AI SELLOFF CONTINUES AFTER BRIEF RESPITE Chipmakers, widely viewed as one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom, led the selloff with the Philadelphia chips index sliding 1.3 per cent. Marvell Technology, which Huang called the "next trillion-dollar company" in June, slumped 3.8 per cent. AI hyperscaler Oracle, which is expanding its cloud AI chip deals with Nvidia, shed 2.6 per cent. Memory chipmaker Micron Technology fell 2.5 per cent and data storage firms Sandisk and Western Digital eased 6 per cent and 3.7 per cent. Photonic product makers Lumentum and Coherent and AI server maker Dell eased between 3 per cent and 5.1 per cent. Construction and power-generation equipment maker Caterpillar and power producer Vistra slipped about 0.5 per cent each. Shares of AMD and Broadcom, which also produce AI chips and compete with Nvidia, however, rose 3.7 per cent and 5.6 per cent, respectively, on expectations that the turmoil at Nvidia could create opportunity for rivals. Other hyperscalers including Alphabet, Amazon.com and Microsoft were also up between 0.8 per cent and 2.7 per cent. AI stocks struggled and the Nasdaq entered a technical correction earlier this month after the Democrats swept the midterm elections, including in states opposed to data centres, stoking fears tighter regulation could slow the AI build-out. Tech-heavy stock markets across the globe witnessed jitters. Japan and South Korea closed nearly 0.7 per cent lower. Tech stocks in Europe were also down about 1 per cent. Nvidia trades at about 12 times its 12-month forward earnings estimates, its lowest since November 2012, according to data compiled by LSEG.

Source: Reuters/rk

PARIS: A bomb alert temporarily disrupted train services at Calais-Fréthun station in northern France on Thursday (Nov 12) morning, affecting both domestic and international rail travel. Train services resumed later on Thursday morning after the gendarmerie authorised their restart, national rail operator SNCF said. The national gendarmerie did not immediately respond to an emailed request for comment. International high-speed rail operator Eurostar said some services between London and Paris had been affected by the disruption, as trains traveling on the route pass through Calais-Fréthun. The incident caused delays to services to and from London, the company said. The alert came amid a broader wave of bomb threats and hoaxes reported in France and other European countries in recent months, targeting flights, schools and, in some cases, media organisations. It was not immediately clear whether Thursday's alert was linked to any of the previous threats.

SINGAPORE: Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed said on Thursday (Nov 12) that it takes compliance obligations under US export control laws "extremely seriously" and that it has cooperated with US inspections. The company has been in the spotlight following reports that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom US authorities suspect of being a Chinese spy. In a statement posted on its website, Megaspeed CEO and Chairman James Tan Yong Pong said: "Compliance is a fundamental priority for the company, and Megaspeed is committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government." Tan said Megaspeed cooperated with inspections by the US Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security and "stands ready to cooperate fully with any other relevant US government authority".

Megaspeed has retained an American law firm to lead a "comprehensive census" of its graphics processing units and independently verify its export control compliance practices, Tan added. The US is looking into the US$4 trillion chipmaker while Nvidia's board is discussing whether to oust Huang following reports of two extramarital affairs, one of which was with the alleged Chinese spy. Separately, Megaspeed on Nov 9 posted on LinkedIn a statement it first issued in December 2025 in response to a Bloomberg report, which it said contained "misleading information and incorrect insinuations" about possible illegal chip transfers. The statement said inspections and reviews by US and Malaysian authorities, as well as Nvidia, found no evidence of illicit chip transfers or other illegal activity. The company added that it did not rule out legal action against Bloomberg. In the comments section, Megaspeed replied “No” when asked whether former executive Alice Huang was a spy.

Related:

What we know about Megaspeed, Singapore-based customer of Nvidia

Who would be next CEO at Nvidia? Top engineer and CFO favoured as candidates

Last October, Singapore police said they were investigating Megaspeed over "suspected breaches of our domestic laws" after a US senator requested the Commerce Department investigate whether Megaspeed had diverted Nvidia chips.  Singapore said last month that the firm was still under investigation. Chinese businesswoman Huang is a former executive at Megaspeed, a company with subsidiaries in Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, the US and Australia. Jensen Huang said on Sunday he had been unfaithful to his wife, but gave no details about the relationship, while Beijing has called the spying claim "a groundless accusation, slander and a smear". Alice Huang could not be reached for comment.

Source: Reuters/dc

MOSCOW: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff arrived in Moscow on Thursday (Nov 12) for talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin , part of their latest push for a peace deal in Ukraine. The Kremlin talks - expected to take place in the first half of the day - will be the 10th time that Witkoff has met Putin in person, and follow two days of trilateral peace talks in Abu Dhabi which finished on Wednesday with news of another planned major prisoner exchange, but no public breakthrough in wider negotiations. Kirill Dmitriev, Putin's special envoy, met Kushner and Witkoff off their plane amid wet snow and accompanied them to central Moscow ahead of their talks with Putin. This week's Abu Dhabi talks were the first direct negotiations between Russia and Ukraine mediated by the US to try to end the four-and-a-half-year-old war in nine months and, although Russian and Ukrainian negotiators reported some progress, the US side said differences remained on major issues, including territory. Despite public optimism from US President Trump, there has been no sign of major compromises. Kyiv has strongly rejected Putin's demands to surrender the whole of the eastern region of Donbas in return for peace, and with talks deadlocked on land, US mediators have tried to steer discussions towards postwar security guarantees and reconstruction. A senior Russian diplomat said on Wednesday that Moscow could conclude non-aggression pacts with NATO member states as part of a new security architecture for Europe, though many European politicians say they oppose any discussion of Europe's overall security before real progress on Ukraine - including a ceasefire - is made.

Source: Reuters/nh
